title: Possibility and deduction
grammar: Might, May, Could, Must (deduction), Can not (deduction)

phases.name: Presentation
phases.content: In this unit you will learn modal verbs to express possibility and deduction: might, may, could, must, can not.

phases.name: Discovery
phases.content: Read these sentences. It might rain later. She may be at home. He could be the new manager. You must be tired. That can not be true. Notice: might/may/could = possibility, must = strong deduction, can not = impossible.

phases.name: Guided practice
phases.prompt: She has not eaten all day. She ___ be hungry.
phases.explanation: When we are sure about something, we use must.

phases.name: Free practice
phases.prompt: Your friend is not answering the phone. Write 3 possible reasons using might, may, could.

phases.name: Mini-test
phases.prompt: He ___ be at home. I saw him leave five minutes ago.
phases.explanation: When something is impossible, we use cannot.
